claims.text: Simultaneous reduction of Pt, Ir, Os, Rh, and Ru precursors enables cooperative nucleation.
Combining multiple noble-metal elements favors formation of single-phase nanoparticles.
The resulting Pt-Ir-Os-Rh-Ru nanoparticles are homogeneous.
Bimetallic precursor systems undergo less synchronized reduction than five-metal precursor systems.
Less synchronized reduction in bimetallic systems increases phase segregation.
Bimetallic nanoparticles consequently have inferior catalytic performance.
The synthesis begins with separately prepared aqueous solutions of cationic and anionic noble-metal precursors.
Mixing preheated anionic and cationic precursor solutions triggers simultaneous reduction and nanoparticle nucleation.
Entropy contributions to phase formation are minimal under the specified low-temperature solution conditions.
The desired mediator is a single-phase nanoparticle in which all constituent metals are randomly distributed.
Controlled cooperative reduction kinetics synchronize nucleation of all metal species and suppress phase segregation.
Uniform dispersion of multiple metals creates a high density of similar active sites.
These active sites stabilize reaction intermediates and optimize binding energies.
Intermediate stabilization and optimized binding energies enhance catalytic performance.
Five-metal HEA nanoparticles will form a more uniform single phase than bimetallic nanoparticles synthesized under comparable conditions.
The HEA nanoparticles will have lower overpotentials and higher current densities than the bimetallic baseline in reactions such as ORR.
The proposed behavior is limited to low-temperature solution reduction of noble-metal systems compositionally similar to Pt-Ir-Os-Rh-Ru.
Kinetic factors dominate phase formation within the stated boundary.
